text: The moon laid silver pathways on the sea.
Sunny walked the warm sand of the bay.
Out of the gentle waves there came a shape,
gliding slow and calm as time itself.
A sea turtle, with a shell like polished stone,
and wise old eyes that twinkled in the light.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “You swim so slow and calm.”
“The sea taught me,” she said. “It never hurries.”
“Come sit with me and watch the moonlit water,
and I will teach you what the ocean knows.”
They watched the waves roll in and slide away,
each one a long slow breath upon the sand.
“Breathe like the sea,” the gentle turtle said.
“In… and out… as slow as rolling waves.”
So Sunny breathed the way the ocean breathes,
and felt herself grow calm and soft and slow.
The turtle's eyes blinked slower, and slower still,
rocked gently by the rhythm of the tide.
She rested on the sand where waves just reached,
the water lapping soft around her shell.
Sunny nestled in the warm dry dune,
still breathing slowly, in and out, like waves.
The bay was still. The moon path stretched to dreams.
Everything was peaceful, deep, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy with the rolling tide.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept the way the ocean sleeps —
slow and deep and gentle as the waves.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, wise sea turtle.
Goodnight, sleepy sea. Goodnight, little one.
